context.synopsis: The House of Representatives passed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1) on May 22, 2025. The card's figures of $880 billion in Medicaid cuts and 8.6 million uninsured do not match these estimates. The enacted version (Public Law 119-21) was scored separately by CBO on July 21, 2025 (net $3.4 trillion deficit increase; 10 million more uninsured in 2034).
context.recovered_rationale: This matters because the legislation paired substantial tax benefits, especially for wealthy recipients, with major reductions to Medicaid and other assistance programs, while increasing projected national debt. The documented coverage losses and cuts to food, education, and clean-energy programs indicate broad distributional consequences. Its significance lies in the scale of the fiscal transfer and the affected public services.
